visual_screen.coverage: all40, frames0/20/40/60/80; selected cases also7/9 frames
visual_screen.qualification: Sparse-frame screening does not certify all-frame temporal quality. Static appearance is a failure only where the prompt requires a process/change. Source-image defects and generated defects must be separated.

architecture_findings.verified: The new physical executor is a full-width pointwise FFN conditioned by C and contextual post-text video state. Video-token interactions still occur in the native self-attention path.
architecture_findings.not_established: Whether lack of independently trainable physical spatiotemporal interaction causes the observed failures; whether learned executor improves over official-body control.
architecture_findings.next_design_question: Evaluate single physical branch with pretrained video-block interaction and semantic grounding against evidence from no-C/official-executor controls. Do not equate more parameters or an expert label with effectiveness.

verified_points: ProPhy physical blocks copy the corresponding video transformer architecture and initial weights.
Its Semantic Expert Block predicts physical-category priors; this is not equivalent to full prompt/action adherence.
PB-only ablation has a limited PC gain and no SA improvement; the combined system has stronger gains.
research.boundary: Different task/backbone/data size/full600 evaluation. It supports a design principle, not a claim that our model will improve.

cross_task_observation: Both A packages lose0.175 PC on matched40 while slightly raising SA; neither improves Joint. Replacing effective direct physics write with a larger pointwise FFN executor did not achieve the target. This does not isolate every changed component.

historical_semantic_branch_check.verified: R15H already retained direct C write and added a C-conditioned query-shift difference over the frozen native text K/V/O. That semantic-response-only addition did not improve its paired16 aggregate.
historical_semantic_branch_check.implication: Do not claim that a generic extra text-query response is new or empirically supported.
